issues.message: The Notifications screen shows an in-app feed with unread dots, 'Mark all read' and swipe-to-dismiss, but the notifications table only models email/sms delivery and has no read/dismissed field or in-app channel.

issues.item: Doctor card attributes vs doctors/users tables
issues.message: The design shows doctor avatar, star rating, years of experience and a doctor gender filter, but neither the doctors nor the users table has photo, rating, experience or gender columns.
The design includes a 'Save Doctor' heart button for favorites, but no requirement or user story covers it and the schema has no table to store saved doctors.

Receptionist is a listed user role (and the design says they see appointments only, with booked_by_user_id in the schema), but the requirements contain no feature, user story or acceptance criteria for receptionist actions such as booking on behalf of patients.

required_fixes: Add an in-app read state (for example is_read/read_at or an 'in_app' channel) to the notifications table, or remove the unread dots, 'Mark all read' and dismiss behaviour from the Notifications screen.
Add the doctor display and filter fields the design uses (photo_url, years_of_experience, rating source, gender) to the schema, or remove them from the Find Doctors and Book Appointment screens.
Either add a favorites requirement and a saved_doctors table, or remove the Save Doctor button from the design.
Add receptionist user stories and acceptance criteria to the requirements and define the receptionist's permitted actions in the design.
recommendations: Make the bottom navigation role-aware, so patients do not see the Dashboard tab and staff see only the tabs relevant to them.
Align the status vocabulary across artifacts: the design's Status Chip uses 'Pending', while the database uses scheduled/confirmed/no_show/rescheduled.
Add a patient-facing profile and personal-details screen to match the patients table, since the registration screen collects only name, email, phone and password.
